title: Offensive recap and transition to defense
ports_note: NONE. Lab 8 is the only lab in the course that serves nothing at all - no model, no listener, no port. The consolidation contract reserved 8008 for an offline worksheet UI; the instructor chose a terminal runner instead on 2026-09-14, so 8008 is deliberately unclaimed and free for part 2.
interaction: beginner (8 guided steps, one of which asks 7 checked questions) or expert (real shell + a blank worksheet filled with nano + mapping.py --grade + check.py)
models_note: NO MODEL. Lab 8 is the only lab since lab 2 that runs no inference, and the only one in the course that needs no ML stack whatsoever. It does not carry the 1.09 GB Qwen GGUF that labs 3-7 share.
python_packages_note: NONE. This is the only lab with no pip layer at all. It imports json, argparse, pathlib, re and urllib - all standard library. Labs 3-7 share a 49.8 MB pip layer; carrying it here would cost every student 49.8 MB for a lab that imports none of it, and the build prompt says so explicitly. This is also why fetch_assets.py reads the ATLAS STIX bundle rather than ATLAS.yaml: the YAML is friendlier but needs PyYAML, and adding a pip layer to save one import is the wrong trade.

lab_assets.note: MITRE ATLAS v2026.08, distilled at build time from the 1,176,189-byte STIX release asset to ~33 KB: 197 techniques with their tactics, parents, CREATION DATES and mitigations; 39 mitigations; 16 tactics in matrix order. PINNED 2026-09-22 (instructor decision): the release-asset URL plus a sha256 that fetch_assets.py verifies, failing the build loudly on mismatch. It previously fetched atlas-navigator-data/main (unpinned), which MITRE deprecated in June 2026 and froze at ATLAS 5.6.0. Descriptions dropped - they are most of the bytes and the lab never prints them. Creation dates kept so beat 7 prints when each unmitigated technique entered ATLAS. SHARED CACHE PATH, and lab 8 is the natural home for ATLAS data in the merged 8-lab image. NOTE: labs 1-7 hard-code their technique IDs in their own text and read nothing at run time, so nothing points at this file yet. Retrofitting them would mean republishing seven images for zero student-visible benefit - not done, and not recommended before the tier rebuild.
lab_assets.rejected_alternative: atlas-navigator-data/dist/stix-atlas-attack-enterprise.json is 39 MB because it carries all of ATT&CK Enterprise, and that repo is deprecated and frozen at 5.6.0 anyway. Lab 8 needs none of it.

lab_assets.note: THIS LAB'S ANSWER KEY, AND IT IS GENERATED RATHER THAN TYPED. lab-research/lab8/gen_course.py reads every student-facing file of labs 1-7 (runner.py, LAB.md, README.md) and refuses to emit a key containing a technique the student was never shown. It caught two real problems on its first run: lab 5's AML.T0085.001 and lab 7's AML.T0096 appear in LAB.md but not in the runner banner, so reading the banner alone would have dropped two techniques and two whole tactics from the coverage picture; and lab 3 writes its fourth technique as the shorthand 'AML.T0051.001 / .002' and never spells the second one out. Re-run it if any lab's text changes. 2026-09-22: regenerated for ATLAS v2026.08 - lab 1's chain now starts AML.T0115 (AML.T0058 was retired), and the part-2 pairings are read from and checked against lab-dev/lab9..lab15's READMEs (lab 1->9, 2->10, 3->12, 4->11, 5->13, 6->14, 7->15).
Written by mapping.py --worksheet. The expert path's mapping exercise with no multiple choice.
What the student answered. check.py reads this, not screen text.
What each step recorded. The runner asserts on this.

THE EVIDENCE. A real ATLAS Navigator layer file - the same format security teams use for their own coverage maps - which loads unmodified at https://atlas.mitre.org/navigator. Instructor decision 2026-09-14: this is the evidence artifact rather than a table of our own design; instructor decision 2026-09-22: students do NOT submit it (whole files cannot go into the class chat) - they review it and prepare questions, and the README carries the link and the three clicks. Both setup scripts copy it out of the container next to lab8-results.txt. 2026-09-22: layer versions 4.5 / navigator 5.3.2 and metadata atlas_data_version 2026.08, matching navigator-atlas_layer_matrix.json in MITRE's v2026.08 release.

not_used.name: a self-hosted ATLAS Navigator
not_used.reason: It is the right tool and its layer format IS this lab's evidence artifact. Not bundled: it is an Angular application needing Node, npm and a hundreds-of-MB toolchain, and serving it needs a port. That breaks 'no new bytes', the single-container rule and the no-port decision, for a 12-minute lab. We adopt the format and link to MITRE's hosted copy.

not_used.name: PyYAML and ATLAS.yaml
not_used.reason: The friendlier format, but it would add the only pip layer in the lab to save one import. The STIX bundle carries the same content and json is stdlib. Measured 2026-09-22: the v2026.08 STIX release asset parses unchanged with the existing parser - 197 techniques, 39 mitigations, 16 tactics; 20/20 course techniques resolve.

not_used.name: the model tier's requirements.txt
not_used.reason: Labs 3-7 share it and lab 8 imports none of it. The build prompt says explicitly not to pull it in for consistency, and it is right: 49.8 MB for nothing.

not_used.name: GenAI-Security-Crosswalk
not_used.reason: An open OWASP-to-ATLAS crosswalk (CC BY-SA 4.0) and the first thing an instructor would reach for. Its header says 'Source list: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025' and this course is on the 2026 list, where the numbering moved - Supply Chain LLM03->LLM04, Excessive Agency LLM06->LLM03, Unbounded Consumption LLM10->LLM06, plus LLM08 Hidden Context Exposure is new. Adopting it would reintroduce the exact numbering bug labs 5, 6 and 7 each corrected by hand. Cited in the debrief with that warning attached.

not_used.name: a defensive tutorial
not_used.reason: INSTRUCTOR DECISION 2026-09-14. This bootcamp is the first half of a two-part course and part 2 carries a one-for-one defender lab for every attack lab. Lab 8 NAMES controls and says what each does in one line - no configuration, no code, no worked examples. A student asking 'yes but HOW?' is told it is a part-2 lab. The temptation is strongest on AML.M0024 and AML.M0033, which each cover five of seven labs, and those are precisely the two that deserve a whole lab rather than a paragraph.

not_used.name: port 8008 and a worksheet UI
not_used.reason: The contract allocates 8008 if this lab serves an offline worksheet UI. Instructor chose the terminal runner 2026-09-14: it matches the other seven labs, needs no port and removes a Windows failure mode. 8008 stays unclaimed.

network: None at run time. No listener, no port, no outbound. Verified with --network none. The ONLY network access in this lab's whole lifecycle is fetch_assets.py during docker build.

measured.note: Measured 2026-09-14, arm64, Docker 29.7.2, on the image built from lab-beta/lab8. ATLAS-derived numbers below re-measured 2026-09-22 on ATLAS v2026.08 (image seclm-labs:lab8-dev built from lab-dev/lab8).
measured.image_on_disk: 230 MB - against 2.64 GB for labs 5-7. The smallest lab in the course.
measured.timing_note: One second, end to end. No model, no inference, no waiting. The 12-15 minute budget is entirely reading time, which is the right shape for a recap and is stated as such in the README.
measured.atlas_distilled: 1,176,189-byte STIX release asset (v2026.08, sha256-checked) -> ~33 KB of JSON. 197 techniques, 39 mitigations, 16 tactics.
measured.course_coverage: 20 distinct techniques across labs 1-7; 13 of ATLAS's 16 tactics (v2026.08 also files AML.T0053 under Lateral Movement; on 5.6.0 it was 12); 8 of the 10 OWASP 2026 entries.
measured.the_spine: AML.T0051.001 LLM Prompt Injection: Indirect appears in 5 of the 7 labs. 12 of the 20 techniques appear in exactly one lab.
measured.top_controls: ATLAS v2026.08: AML.M0035 AI Red Team touches 7 of 7 labs; AML.M0020 Generative AI Guardrails 6 of 7; AML.M0024 AI Telemetry Logging and AML.M0033 Input and Output Validation for AI Agent Components 5 of 7 each.
measured.the_gap: ATLAS v2026.08: 2 of the 20 techniques have NO published mitigation - AML.T0065 LLM Prompt Crafting (added 2025-03-12, supporting step in labs 4 and 5) and AML.T0110 AI Agent Tool Poisoning (added 2026-03-30, lab 6's core). On ATLAS 5.6.0 it was 9; 7 of those 9 gained a mitigation in v2026.08, mostly broad ones (M0020 closes 4, M0000 2, the new M0035 2). Matrix-wide, 73 of 197 techniques still have none. This is the lab's ending and the hand-off to part 2: the standard moved fast, covered is not the same as solved, and the remaining gap is the agent tool layer.
measured.peak_ram: negligible - Python plus a 24 KB JSON file. Verified at --memory=1200m for consistency with the other labs.
measured.determinism: trivially deterministic - no model, no randomness, no clock in any output.
measured.published_layer_sharing: TO BE VERIFIED on the published manifest.
